question: A 62-year-old woman with advanced cervical cancer reports severe pain (NRS 8/10) despite being on regular tramadol for 2 weeks. She has no renal impairment. According to the WHO analgesic ladder, what is the MOST appropriate next step?

answers.text: Add paracetamol to the tramadol regimen and reassess in 2 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paracetamol can be continued as an adjuvant but simply adding it does not address the failure of a Step 2 weak opioid for severe pain (NRS 8/10). The patient has progressed beyond Step 2.

answers.text: Switch to oral morphine (strong opioid) at an appropriate starting dose, with breakthrough provision

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NRS 8/10 pain uncontrolled on a weak opioid = WHO ladder Step 3 indication. Start oral morphine 5–10 mg every 4 hours (regular dosing) with 1/6th of the daily dose available as a breakthrough dose every hour as needed. Titrate upward by 30–50% every 24–48 hours.

answers.text: Refer directly to radiotherapy for pain control before prescribing opioids

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Radiotherapy can be an excellent analgesic for bone pain but it takes weeks to work and requires planning. Pharmacological pain control (WHO ladder Step 3) must be initiated immediately — do not delay opioids pending radiotherapy.

answers.text: Prescribe fentanyl transdermal patch as first strong opioid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fentanyl patches are not appropriate for opioid-naive patients or for rapidly titrating acute severe pain — the patch has a 12–24 hour lag to steady state and cannot be titrated daily. Oral morphine is the preferred first strong opioid for WHO Step 3 initiation.

overallFeedback.feedback: WHO analgesic ladder Step 3: severe or Step-2-uncontrolled pain = strong opioid. Oral morphine is the gold standard starting agent — regular 4-hourly dosing with 1/6th daily dose breakthrough.
Correct. Severe pain (NRS ≥7) uncontrolled on Step 2 = WHO ladder Step 3: strong opioid (oral morphine), regular dosing + breakthrough provision. Fentanyl patch is not for de novo initiation.
